label: digit 3 input at original positions 3-6
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 3 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t = 3..6. It fires at about 99.9% of such steps and nowhere else: never on 3 at t = 0-2 or t >= 7, never on any other token, and never in the delimiter or copy phases (including when 3 is fed back as a copy input). Position modulates magnitude: by activation-mass share relative to count, t = 4 and 5 are strongest, t = 3 is moderate, and t = 6 is weakest. Top activations are around t = 4. Previous tokens, first token and L have little effect. The rare false positives are at t = 6, mostly in sequences that contain repeated tokens.

issues: Minor: the reported test precision of 1 is rounded. The actual test precision is 0.99955, with 22 false positives out of 49405 predicted steps, and the test F1 is 0.99978. All 22 false positives are at t=6. They are scattered across different token histories and look like noise near the activation threshold at the weakest position, not a systematic class.

I checked every factual claim against the dev profile. The feature never fires in the delimiter or copy phase (0 active steps in each). It never fires at t=0-2 or t>=7. Every activation is on in_tok=3. Recall at orig_idx 3-6 is about 0.034/0.25, which matches nearly all 3s at those positions. Mass per activation is about 1.24e-5 at t=3, 2.9e-5 at t=4, 2.7e-5 at t=5 and 1.07e-5 at t=6, consistent with t=4 and 5 strongest, t=3 moderate and t=6 weakest. On the test split there are 0 missed activations.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
